correctness.rationale: A finite connected graph in the three-state threshold-one GHM has no nonzero fixed point; any nonconstant time-zero three-periodic configuration forces every vertex to rotate through 0,1,2 and satisfies a neighbor-in-successor-phase condition. Direct successor arrows must end on a directed cycle of length divisible by three. In singly resonant cactus the unique core cycle supports six phase/orientation configurations and child-block successor arrows cannot point away from the core without producing another resonant cycle. Bridges force one phase; each rooted noncore simple cycle has 2floor(ℓ/3)+1 phase extensions by the two complete weak increment-word families with modulo-three closure. Multiplying proves the claimed product; no resonant cycle yields zero. Independently brute-forced all 3-color configurations for cycles length 3..9, a triangle+square (18 states), and nested triangle+square+pentagon (54 states). Actual verify_global.py and verify_local.py read: proper synchronous update and rooted-cycle DP. Finite tests supplement general block-tree reasoning.
